summary: USB-C PD negotiation failing after BIOS config push causing dock/charging/provisioning disruptions
description: Issue summary: After a recent company-wide BIOS configuration baseline pushed via SCCM, a subset of laptops connected to corporate USB-C docks intermittently fail Power Delivery (PD) negotiation and do not enumerate peripherals. Impact: Users experience no charging while docked, external monitors not detected, and some devices fail to complete enrollment during zero-touch provisioning, blocking new-hire workstation setup and on-desk productivity. Environment: Observed on Dell Latitude 9440 and Lenovo ThinkPad X1 Gen 11 devices in prod-us-west and prod-eu-west. BIOS baseline applied on 2026-03-09. Problem first reported by onboarding team 2026-03-10.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start with device on battery (20-60%). 2) Attach company-branded USB-C dock (firmware v1.3.2). 3) Observe power LED and battery state; watch dmesg/syslog and Windows Event Viewer for device enumeration events. 4) On affected devices, PD negotiation fails within 3-8 seconds and laptops remain on battery; on others PD succeeds. 5) Reboot or hot-unplug/re-plug may temporarily restore PD for some devices.
logs: Windows Event IDs: Kernel-PnP 219, Kernel-Power 41 (some occurrences). UEFI logs on affected units show ACPI: PD_PORT_HANDLER error codes and USB PD negotiation timeout. Dock debug logs (partner) show 'NO_SINK_CAPS' followed by repeated 'PD_RETRY' entries. SCCM deployment logs show BIOS baseline applied successfully to host IDs prior to failure window.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Aisha Patel: Report from onboarding - two new hires could not finish autopilot; laptop showed no battery charging when dock attached. Escalating to infra eng.
2026-03-10 11:05 - Ethan Blake: Confirmed repro on Dell 9440 with baseline v2026-03-bios. Collecting UEFI debug screenshots and requesting vendor USB-C controller logs.
2026-03-11 08:43 - Diego Morales (SCCM): Baseline rollout used new ACPI settings (DisableLegacyPD=1). Rolling patch plan created to test reverting setting on small cohort.

2026-03-11 15:20 - Hardware Vendor (Dock Team): Dock firmware shows PD requests but reports sink caps mismatch with host when DisableLegacyPD is toggled. Asking for host-side PD controller firmware version.

2026-03-12 10:02 - Ethan Blake: Narrowed to machines with Intel PD controller fw 2.7.1. Machines with newer PD fw 2.8.0 do not reproduce. Started coordinated validation to flash PD controller fw on test bench.
2026-03-12 16:30 - Priya Nair: Onboarding blocked for 5 new hires today; using temporary USB-A chargers and hot-desking workaround. Tracking impact for ops.
2026-03-12 17:10 - Security (Jessie Kwan): Confirmed no data exfil or security alert correlated; this is a hardware/UEFI negotiation regression.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: New BIOS baseline flips an ACPI/PD compatibility flag (DisableLegacyPD) which interacts poorly with Intel PD controller fw 2.7.1, causing the host to advertise incompatible sink capabilities. Evidence: Repro on multiple units with identical PD fw; units with PD fw 2.8.0 unaffected. SCCM logs show BIOS setting toggled at baseline rollout. Vendor dock logs show 'NO_SINK_CAPS' which aligns with host failing to respond to PD contract requests. Next steps: (1) Create test group to revert BIOS setting on small cohort. (2) Coordinate PD controller firmware flash to 2.8.0 on failing devices. (3) Request dock vendor to provide tolerant fallback for legacy hosts if possible. (4) Add hardware inventory check to provisioning pipeline to avoid blocked autopilot with known PD fw versions.
resolution: Workaround: Reverted BIOS DisableLegacyPD flag in SCCM for impacted device collection and queued a staged rollback for devices with PD fw 2.7.1. For immediate onboarding, provisioning team used USB-A chargers and manual imaging for 7 affected hires. Permanent fix: Coordinated with hardware vendor to produce PD controller firmware 2.8.0 image; SRE scheduled PD firmware update for affected asset tag range and added post-flash verification steps. Also updated the BIOS baseline playbook to skip toggling PD compatibility flags until PD controller fw compatibility is validated. Follow-up: Runbook updated and a small audit scheduled to detect devices with PD fw <=2.7.1 before future BIOS pushes.
